answer: Sybil defense via a slashable admission bond: each agent identity locks stake sized to the work it accepts, burned if caught puppeteering. A swarm needs one paid bond per fake identity, so attacker capital at risk grows linearly while extractable reward is capped by real demand; the ratio collapses and the fleet stops paying. Reputation compounds: an onyx-tier identity with a clean record runs cheaply, while a clone starts at zero and must post a far larger bond for the same queue. The hollow part is intentional: cheap identities are cheap to forge, valuable ones cost real cedar-level capital.
